decisions.reason: Close to the established electrometer/QA core and a flagship, its option value remains high and unlikely to be abandoned.
Building on established oncology software and still having unresolved upside, the option is worth keeping at low carrying cost.
The CT phantom is close to the established medical imaging line and launched only in 2024, so uncertainty remains high while keeping costs are low.
Distant from the firm's core dosimetry/radiation QA and not a flagship, its option value is lower and resources are better shifted to closer options.
This full-field mammography phantom is likewise distant from existing capabilities and faces many competing options, so continued commitment is less justified.
As a flagship product line building directly on the established medical imaging QA offer, its option value is high and the firm is likely to keep investing.
